title: PM Modi urges self-reliance, calls upon citizens to realise 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
• August 15, 2026 11:14
    Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke hoists the national flag at his native village in Maharashtra

    Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke hoists the national flag at his native village in Maharashtra on August 15, 2026. Mr. Dipke on said that government-run schools in India remain neglected irrespective of parties in power as he prepared to launch ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign from Hingoli in Maharashtra, marking Independence Day.

  • August 15, 2026 10:59
    Slogans that built solidarity during freedom struggle

    Slogans are dispatches, a voice of persuasion and resistance, and hence, carry as much historical and cultural value as our monuments. Though the trajectory of sloganeering has evolved with time, the essence of its purpose is still the same — bringing change.

    Going viral: Slogans that built solidarity during freedom struggle

    Explore how powerful slogans united India’s diverse voices in the struggle for independence, shaping national identity and resistance.

  • August 15, 2026 10:45
    Looking back: Why Chennai journalists went on a fast on Independence Day 25 years ago?

    On the morning of August 15, 2001, as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister J. Jayalalithaa hoisted the national flag at Fort St. George, about 3.5 km away, scores of journalists sat on a fast outside the M.A. Chidambaram Cricket Stadium, near the State Guest House in Chennai.

    About 48 hours earlier, several journalists, particularly photographers and camerapersons, had been subjected to a savage attack by the police just outside the office of the Director General of Police on Dr. Radhakrishnan Salai.

    Read the full article here,
  • August 15, 2026 10:11
    Watch: Independence Day celebrations from across the country

    Independence Day celebrations are under way across the country. Here are glimpses from a few States:

  • August 15, 2026 10:01
    Modi urges all to join 100-day anti-drug campaign

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a collective effort to make India drug-free, urging families to join the 100-day nationwide Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan.

    In his address to the nation on the 80th Independence Day, Modi said drug addiction has emerged as a major challenge for the country’s youth, and stressed the need to tackle it.

    “Drug addiction is becoming a very big challenge for the country and its youth. Making India drug-free should be a collective responsibility of all of us,” he said from the ramparts of the Red Fort.

    “For our bright future, our youth generation should be strong, our youth should be capable and should work for the country,” he said.

    Mr. Modi urged volunteers, NGOs, social and cultural organisations and spiritual leaders to prepare for the 100-week campaign for a drug-free India.

    -PTI

  • August 15, 2026 09:54
    PM Modi's I-Day speech shortest in four years

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered a 75-minute Independence Day speech on Saturday (Augst 15, the shortest in four years and his fourth shortest ever.

    On India’s 79th Independence Day last year, Modi had delivered a 103-minute speech, breaking his own record of a 98-minute address delivered on the 78th Independence Day in 2024.

    His longest Independence Day speech before 2024 was for 96 minutes in 2016, while his shortest speech was in 2017, when he spoke for 56 minutes.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 09:37
    'Dimagi Naxals' looking to create unrest, must identify, isolate them: Modi

    Maoist extremism is breathing its last in the country, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, as he called for “identifying and isolating” the “dimagi Naxals”.

    Addressing the nation on the 80th Independence Day, the Prime Minister said Naxalism and Maoism destroyed the future of several youths.

    “For four decades, huge areas and people were in their clutches under the fear of guns. Over 3,500 security personnel died protecting people; the number is higher than those who die in war,” he said.

    “When we came to power in 2014, we swore to rid the country of Naxals. I am happy Maoist violence is taking its last breath,” he said, adding that several areas have become free of Naxalites and are becoming developed.

    Mr. Modi added, “For years, those with Naxal mentality had their place in the power corridors. They were in government committees as advisors. Maoist thinking impacted policies.

    “We have succeeded in getting rid of armed Naxals in the jungles, but ‘dimagi Naxals’ are looking for opportunities to create violence, unrest … They want to drag the society on the wrong path,” he said.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 09:17
    Modi announces free online coaching for youth

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced free online coaching for aspirants preparing for competitive exams to ease the financial burden on their families.

    “Coaching classes burden the poor and the middle class. We will provide free online coaching for various exams,” Mr. Modi said in his address to the nation on India’s 80th Independence Day.

    “Every parent feels that if they do not send their child to a coaching class, they are not a prestigious family,” he said.

    The Prime Minister said he assures these families that they can save “thousands of crores of rupees” spent on coaching, be close to their children, and care for them.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 09:10
    Added 650 new universities, doubled medical seats, since 2014: Modi

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country added 650 new universities in the last decade and more than doubled the number of medical seats since 2014.

    In his address to the nation on the 80th Independence Day, Modi said the government brought in a new education policy after decades.

    “For 35 years, there was no education policy. We brought a new education policy,” he said from the ramparts of the Red Fort.

    “From 2004 to 2014, there were fewer than 350 universities. And today, within 10-12 years, nearly 650 new universities have been added,” the Prime Minister said.

    “Before 2014, there were only 400 medical seats, and today nearly 850 medical seats are available,” he added.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 09:01
    PM Modi appeals to all parties to support 33% reservation for women in Parliament

    In his speech, Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to all parties to extend their support for Women’s reservation in Parliament and Assemblies. 

    “33% reservation for women is call of the hour, appeal to all parties to support and take credit for it,” he said. 

  • August 15, 2026 08:46
    Centre, state, industry must work together for Viksit Bharat: Modi

    The Centre, the state, and the industry must work together for reforms, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday.

    In his address to the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort, Modi said that society, government, and industry must change their traditional ways, thinking, and targets to achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047.

    “Things that have not been done in the last five or six decades, we have to do them in the next five to seven years. I have faith in my country’s youth, farmers, labourers, daughters, and mothers to be able to do this,” he said.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 08:36
    PM Modi highlights railway electrification, green hydrogen train

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted the pace of railway electrification under his government, saying 70% of the network was electrified in 10 years compared with 30% in the previous 90 years.

    Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, Mr. Modi said railway electrification had begun in 1925 but only 30% of the network was electrified in the next 90 years.

    “We completed 100% electrification in just one decade. Thirty per cent in 90 years and 70% in 10 years -- this is the pace of work,” he said.

    He said electrification has helped save imported diesel and benefited the environment as trains are increasingly powered by electricity.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 08:22
    Trade agreements we are signing provide big opportunity for MSMEs: PM Modi

    PM Modi asked MSMEs not to let go of opportunities being provided by the trade agreements being signed by the country. 

    “World has started recognising our abilities; we have concluded FTAs with 40 countries,” he said, adding that markets of world open for Indian farmers, we have to reach there. “Our agri-products must become global brands.”

    “There should be no compromise with quality, our mantra should be ‘quality, quality, quality’.”

  • August 15, 2026 08:17
    Proved naysayers wrong by ensuring sufficient energy supplies during West Asia crisis: PM Modi

    When West Asia crisis happened, some people tried to scare us that we will not get petrol, diesel or LPG, PM Modi says during his address, adding that his government proved naysayers wrong by ensuring sufficient energy supplies. 

    “Some people weaponised systems at their disposal during times of crisis, but our self-reliance helped us.” 

    “Due to our measures there is no shortage of gas, fuel, urea in country today,” he added. 

  • August 15, 2026 08:11
    India moving forward on harnessing alternative sources of energy: PM Modi

    PM Modi said India is moving forward on harnessing alternative sources of energy. 

    “We have set target of 200 GW nuclear energy, setting up 5 new nuclear reactors,” he said, adding that over 50 lakh households in country now covered by solar energy. 

    Piped gas is reaching 1.75 crore households today, he said.

  • August 15, 2026 08:07
    PM Modi assures flood, landslide-hit families of government support

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured families affected by floods and landslides in several parts of the country that the government stands with them and shares their pain.

    Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort after hoisting the national flag on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, Modi said, “My dear Indians, in the past few days, some parts of the country have witnessed floods and landslides, and many families have been affected. We fully understand their pain and suffering. I assure the affected families that the entire country stands with them.” He expressed solidarity with those affected by the natural calamities.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 08:05
    Energy security is the demand of our times: PM Modi

    Saying that Energy security is the demand of our times, PM Modi added that his Government has taken several steps for this. 

    Mr. Modi also urged self-reliance, saying “We cannot remain dependent on other nations.”

    “Many countries are now depending on India for critical minerals,” he said adding that India has set up semi-conductor plants in its bid to become ‘aatmanirbhar’

  • August 15, 2026 07:56
    We must dream big, because big dreams expand our thinking and broaden the horizons of our vision: PM Modi

    Addressing the nation from ramparts of Red Fort, PM Modi, says, “A nation becomes great and achieves its aspirations when it moves forward on the strength of its dreams, its resolve and its capabilities. My fellow citizens, our country can no longer be driven by small dreams. We must dream big, because big dreams expand our thinking and broaden the horizons of our vision. Our resolve must be firm. When our resolve is strong, the ability to find a way through difficulties and disasters emerges on its own.”

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 07:51
    5,000 special guests from diverse backgrounds attend 80th I-Day celebrations

    Nearly 5,000 special guests from different walks of life, including women entrepreneurs, young innovators, farmers and beneficiaries of various government schemes, are in attendance at the 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort.

    The invitees included International Yoga Day volunteers, women entrepreneurs under the PM Mudra Yojana, beneficiaries of schemes including NAMASTE, PM AJAY and SEED, and best performing My Bharat volunteers.

    Best performing beneficiaries of PMAY(U), street vendors under PM SVANidhi, urban sanitation workers under the Swachh Bharat Mission, best performing Delhi Metro workers, workers associated with Kartavya Path and Central Vista, staff of government hospitals in Delhi were also part of the gathering.

    The special guests also included young innovators under national innovation programmes, scientists in different fields, cab drivers of Bharat Taxi in Delhi, interns under the Prime Minister Internship Scheme, and best performing start-ups supported under various government schemes.

    - PTI

  • August 15, 2026 07:47
    'We must realise the dream of Viksit Bharat by 2047': PM Modi

    During his address to the nation, PM Modi calls upon Indian citizens to realise the dream of Viksit Bharat by 2047. 

    Mr. Modi says that despite gaining freedom in 1947, the country couldn’t gain speed towards becoming a developed country. 

  • August 15, 2026 07:42
    Watch LIVE: PM Modi addresses the nation on Independence Day
  • August 15, 2026 07:41
    PM Modi begins address

    PM Modi has begun his addresses to the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort in New Delhi. 

    Prior to the this, for the first time, the National Song, ‘Vande Mataram’, was rendered during the Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort.

  • August 15, 2026 07:13
    PM Modi pays floral tributes at Rajghat
  • August 15, 2026 07:03
    India's constitutional values, democratic institutions have faced serious challenges: Kharge

    Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said India’s constitutional values, democratic institutions and social harmony have faced “serious challenges” over the last 10 years, as he called for full measure of equality and justice for the economically-weaker sections.

    In his message to people on India’s 80th Independence Day, Mr. Kharge said the country has travelled a long way, but many aspirations still remain unfulfilled.

  • August 15, 2026 07:01
    PM Modi greets people on Independence Day

    Prime Minister Narendra Modi greeted people on the occasion of Independence Day and said powered by 140 crore Indians, the country is scaling new heights of progress across different sectors.

    Mr. Modi also paid tributes to the countless freedom fighters whose courage, sacrifice and unwavering commitment ensured the end of colonial rule.

title: In a first, Vande Mataram rendered during 80th Independence Day celebrations at Red Fort
author: PTI
content_html:
In a first for Independence Day celebrations, 'Vande Mataram' was rendered at the Red Fort complex during the 79th anniversary of the historic occasion on August 15, followed by the recitation of the national anthem at the grand event.

The mega function commemorates 150 years of the enduring legacy of the national song, 'Vande Mataram', as floral decoration on the ramparts depicted the national flag at the centre flanked by 'Vande Mataram' in Hindi.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the 80th Independence Day celebrations at the Red Fort amid patriotic fervour and multi-layer security.

An Army band played the tune of 'Vande Mataram' as the guests present on the occasion sung the national song. This was followed by the Prime Minister hoisting the national flag, and then the national anthem was recited.

After the flag hoisting, the tricolour received a 'Rashtriya Salute'.

After that, flower petals were be showered at the venue by two Mi-17 helicopters of the Indian Air Force -- one trooping the national flag and the other carrying a flag depicting 'Vande Mataram'.

Written in 1875 by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, 'Vande Mataram' had turned into a rallying cry during the freedom movement. It was adopted as India's national song by the Constituent Assembly in 1950.

The government last November launched a year-long celebration to mark 150 years of 'Vande Mataram'.

'Vande Mataram' was initially composed independently and later included in Chatterjee's novel 'Anandamath'. It was first sung by Rabindranath Tagore at the 1896 Congress Session in Calcutta (now Kolkata).

The chant 'Vande Mataram' as a political slogan was first used on August 7, 1905, according to a note '150 Years of Vande Mataram: A Melody That Became a Movement', shared by the government on November 6 last year.

'Vande Mataram' was first published in the literary journal 'Bangadarshan' on November 7, 1875. Later, Chatterjee incorporated the hymn in his novel 'Anandamath', which was published in 1882. It was set to music by Tagore, it said.

Published - August 15, 2026 08:41 am IST

title: PM Modi warns of weaponisation of resources, sea routes; urges energy self-reliance
author: PTI
content_html:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (August 15, 2026) warned that the weaponisation of resources and strategic sea routes by some countries posed risks to India's economic security, calling for greater self-reliance in energy to reduce the country's vulnerability to overseas supplies.

Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on India's 80th Independence Day, Mr. Modi said India needed to strengthen domestic capacity in critical areas, including energy and minerals, as geopolitical tensions increasingly exposed the risks of dependence on external sources.

Without naming any country, Mr. Modi said resources ranging from fuel and medicines to technology were increasingly being used as instruments of geopolitical pressure, while strategic geographical routes were also being weaponised.

His remarks come against the backdrop of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Tehran's retaliation, which has severely disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key conduit for global energy supplies.

The narrow waterway between Iran and Oman handled about 20 million barrels per day of oil and petroleum products in 2025, equivalent to roughly a quarter of global seaborne oil trade, according to the International Energy Agency. It also carried almost 20% of global LNG trade, leaving major Asian importers particularly exposed to any prolonged disruption.

The conflict has sharply reduced maritime traffic through the strait and pushed up energy and shipping costs. Renewed tanker attacks have stalled efforts to resolve the conflict.

For India, the disruption has highlighted the risks posed by its dependence on imported energy. The country has had to seek alternative LNG supplies from countries including Oman, the United States, Nigeria and Angola after uncertainty over Gulf shipments, while Indian refiners have also moved to diversify crude purchases.

India has already broadened its energy sourcing, importing crude from 41 countries and LNG from 15, up from 27 and six respectively, as New Delhi seeks to insulate the economy from geopolitical shocks.

The Strait of Hormuz is particularly important to India because much of the energy passing through it is bound for Asia. The IEA estimates that India received nearly half of its crude oil that transited the strait in 2025. It also obtained almost two-thirds of its LNG supplies through the waterway.

Modi on becoming self-reliant in energy

Mr. Modi said the geopolitical conflicts have underscored the importance of becoming self-reliant in energy.

India, which imports nearly 90% of its crude oil requirements and about half of its natural gas needs, is seeking to tap its largely underexplored offshore reserves as part of a broader push to strengthen energy security, he said, citing the recently approved the ₹84,084-crore Samudra Manthan National Offshore Exploration Scheme, aimed at accelerating exploration for oil and gas in deepwater and ultra-deepwater areas over the next five years.

The programme will support seismic surveys, exploratory drilling and shared offshore infrastructure, with the government seeking to attract greater investment and technology into India's offshore basins.

Mr. Modi said the government has also opened up 99% of India's sedimentary basins for oil and gas exploration and production, expanding access to areas that were previously largely off-limits to commercial exploration. The move is intended to unlock domestic hydrocarbon resources and reduce India's exposure to global energy-price and supply shocks.

The Prime Minister went on to list achievements of his government in the last 12 years - expansion of piped cooking gas coverage from 70 cities to 700 cities, with the fuel - an alternate to LPG which is largely imported from the West Asia - now being supplied to 1.75 crore households as against 22 lakh in 2014.

Also, generation of electricity from the sun's solar energy has jumped to 160 gigawatt from 2 gigawatt a decade back, he said.

Energy security has emerged as a central element of Mr. Modi's broader push for an "Atmanirbhar Bharat", or self-reliant India. The government has also sought to expand domestic exploration of critical minerals and increase the role of nuclear power and other non-fossil energy sources.

In 2024-25, crude oil imports were valued at about $137 billion, while petroleum products and LNG imports were worth $24 billion and $15 billion respectively.

title: Jharkhand student protesters plan ‘Tiranga Yatra’ to spread message of unity
author: Amit Bhelari
content_html:
Students protesting against alleged irregularities in Jharkhand’s recruitment examinations are planning to take out a ‘Tiranga Yatra’ to celebrate India’s 80th Independence Day in Ranchi on Saturday (August 15, 2026).

JPSC-JSSC Reform Manch leader Ravindra Paswan said the “indefinite” protest, which entered its 21st day on Friday, will continue until the government accepted their demands.

“On Independence Day, we have organised a Tiranga Yatra. Students from all districts of Jharkhand will come here to participate in this march. The aim is to convey a message of unity and patriotism,“ Mr. Paswan said.

Kumar Rajat, Sub-Divisional Officer of Ranchi Sadar, and Dhananjay Kumar, Additional District Magistrate (Law and Order), went to the protest site to gather information about the march.

The march will begin at 9.30 a.m. from Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where the students are camping, and will pass through Kachhari Chowk, Nucleus Mall, Lalpur Chowk, Plaza Chowk, Firayalal Chowk, and Shaheed Chowk before returning to the stadium, the students said.

Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Kumar Mahto, in a video message from the Ranchi Sadar Hospital, alleged that a few people were trying to “weaken” the protest. He urged protesting students to continue with the agitation for the “sake of reforms” in competitive examinations.

“I am under treatment at Sadar Hospital, Ranchi and continuing my hunger strike. Today is the 12th day. After the lathi-charge during the Vidhan Sabha March on August 10, I was brought to Sadar Hospital, and it has been four days now,” Mr. Mahto said in the video posted on X.

“I have been continuously urging the hospital management of Ranchi Sadar to transfer me to the protest venue, Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, where my student friends are sitting in a peaceful protest,” he added.

Mr. Mahto demanded an inquiry into the lathi-charge on students during the August 10 rally. “I demand legal action against the official responsible for giving the order of lathi-charge,” he said, adding that the protesting students should not worry about his health. 

Also Read: Agitating students accuse govt. of withholding health details of Devendra Mahto to weaken stir

“At present, the most important thing is the reform in the recruitment process, which has collapsed in Jharkhand. It is really painful that in every exam, there is a paper leak, irregularities and jobs are being offered on recommendations,” he said.

Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on hunger strike for the past 13 days to protest alleged irregularities, is undergoing treatment at Sadar Hospital, in Ranchi | Photo Credit: PTI

He added that the “soul of Jharkhand is being sold” with these jobs. “Jharkhand is in danger, and you all have to save it. I will appeal to the officials of the State government that power comes and goes in democracy. Do not become a slave and follow the instructions of the government blindly,” Mr. Mahto said.

In a related development, the police continued examining video footage to identify miscreants involved in violence during the Vidhan Sabha March on Monday (August 10). The police have registered FIRs against more than 500 unnamed protesters.

title: PM Modi assures flood, landslip-hit families of government support
author: PTI
content_html:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (August 15, 2026) assured families affected by floods and landslips in several parts of the country that the government stands with them and shares their pain.

Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort after hoisting the national flag on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day, Mr. Modi said, "My dear Indians, in the past few days, some parts of the country have witnessed floods and landslides, and many families have been affected. We fully understand their pain and suffering. I assure the affected families that the entire country stands with them." He expressed solidarity with those affected by the natural calamities.

This year, heavy monsoon rains and flash floods have affected several parts of the country, including Assam, Kerala, Uttarakhand and Nagaland. Rains have caused flooding and landslips in several areas, affecting people and disrupting normal life.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (August 15, 2026) greeted people on the occasion of Independence Day and said powered by 140 crore Indians, the country is scaling new heights of progress across different sectors.

title: MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck: No significant environmental impact on Lakshadweep islands and coastal areas, says NCSCM research
author: G. Krishnakumar
content_html:
A comprehensive assessment carried out by the Chennai-based National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM) on the potential environmental impact on the Lakshadweep islands following the sinking of the container vessel MSC Elsa 3 off the Kerala coast on May 25, 2025 has found that the shipwreck did not result in measurable ecological or socioeconomic damage to the archipelago.

However, the incident has underscored the inherent vulnerability of remote island ecosystems to maritime accidents and highlighted the importance of strengthening maritime incident preparedness through early warning systems, island-specific contingency planning, co-ordinated inter-agency response mechanisms and sustained environmental monitoring to enhance resilience against future spill risks, according to the research based on field surveys, lab-based analysis, remote sensing, numerical spill trajectory modelling and stakeholder consultations at Kalpeni and Andrott islands.

The study was carried out as per the directives issued by the Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal after it took suo motu cognisance of the report titled ‘Containers from sunken ship likely to drift towards Alappuzha, Kollam Coasts in 48 hours: INCOIS’ published in The Hindu.

The tribunal had asked the Union Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways to submit the details of States and Union Territories that may have suffered environmental damage following the shipwreck.

The Lakshadweep islands, characterised by ecologically-sensitive coral reefs, lagoons and seagrass ecosystems warranted a precautionary, science-based assessment to evaluate the impact caused by the shipwreck located approximately 38 nautical miles off the Kerala coast at a depth of about 51 m.

The vessel had went down with 640 containers, including 13 with hazardous cargo and 12 with calcium carbide. A large quantity of pellets, also called nurdles, had washed ashore on the southern coast following the incident.

A report prepared by the NCSCM under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on the potential environmental and socio-economic risks of the incident on the Lakshadweep islands stated that multiple lines of evidence indicated that physiochemical parameters of seawater and sediments, including nutrients, heavy metals and polycyclic acromatic hydrocarbons remained within the natural baseline ranges characteristic of coral atoll environments.

Biological assessments further confirmed the absence of stress or degradation in plankton communities, benthic assemblages, coral reefs, seagrass meadows and associated lagoonal habitats, it said.

The marine litter and microplastic observations by the researchers reflected background conditions linked to chronic regional sources rather than incident-specific inputs. The socio-economic evaluations demonstrated that fisheries operations, access to fishing grounds, catch composition and tourism activities continued uninterrupted as there was no reported livelihood losses or adverse community impacts.

Numerical modelling of spill fate and transport indicated that contaminants associated with the shipwreck did not reach the Lakshadweep coastal or lagoonal environment during the assessment period, it said.

The research found that the Lakshadweep’s small, low-lying coral islands faced inherent constraints in waste handling owing to limited land availability, fragile groundwater systems, high tourism pressure and dependence on imported goods. The findings emphasised that conventional mainland-centric waste systems are unsuitable, necessitating decentralised, low-footprint and circular economy-oriented solutions tailored to island conditions.

The way forward required strengthening maritime incident preparedness through early-warning systems, season-specific spill response planning, enhanced surveillance along the key corridors including the Nine Degree channel, according to the study.

title: A.P.’s Mega DSC-2025: What are the allegations and how has the government responded? | Explained
author: P. Sujatha Varma
content_html:
The “Mega” DSC-2025 recruitment for 16,347 teaching posts in Andhra Pradesh has come under scrutiny, with the Opposition YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) and a section of candidates raising questions over the conduct of the examination, merit lists, certificate verification, horizontal reservation and the Sports Quota.

Also read | DSC-2025 conducted with transparency and fairness, says Education Secretary

The controversy has led to 335 cases being filed in courts, including 69 related to the Sports Quota, three cases in the Supreme Court and three PILs concerning various aspects of the recruitment process. YSRCP has stepped up its protests, demanding a CBI probe and the resignation of Human Resource Development Minister Nara Lokesh.

The School Education Department, however, has rejected the allegations of irregularities, maintaining that the recruitment was conducted through a technology-driven and rule-based process. Officials have attributed several of the complaints to individual grievances and differences in the interpretation of the revised horizontal reservation methodology.

How have the roles been merged?

YSRCP has questioned the departure from the earlier practice of entrusting question-paper preparation to the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) and examination conduct to the DSC Convenor. YSRCP MLC Parvathareddy Chandrasekhar Reddy, who filed a PIL in the High Court seeking a CBI probe, alleged that assigning both functions to SCERT compromised the transparency of the recruitment process.

The Government, however, said the decision was taken to improve coordination and avoid delays. It explained that the Joint Director (Teacher Eligibility Test and Teacher Recruitment Test) oversees the administrative aspects of recruitment, including schedules, vacancies, G.Os., notifications, applications, examinations, answer keys, certificate verification, selection lists and results. The Director, SCERT, on the other hand, handles the confidential academic work, including subject expert committees, question banks, mock tests, answer keys and objections.

According to the Government, combining the two responsibilities under one officer facilitated quicker decision-making and coordination, helping complete the recruitment process in a record 148 days, within the prescribed timelines.

What is the controversy over Purama Naveen’s candidature?

Questions over the recruitment process intensified after the name of Purama Naveen, an outsourced employee of SCERT, figured in the initial merit lists. This led to allegations that persons associated with the examination system could have had access to question banks or other confidential information.

The School Education Department has rejected the allegations, stating that the examination was conducted entirely in Computer Based Test (CBT) mode, with encrypted systems, restricted access, randomised question-paper allocation and multiple sessions. It said different question papers were used across sessions and that no evidence-backed official complaint of question-paper leakage had been received.

Mr. Naveen had initially figured at Rank 1 in the Krishna district School Assistant-Social Studies merit list and Rank 6 in the Zone-II TGT-Telugu list, but his name was subsequently removed from the revised merit list. His candidate login was reportedly blocked and he was not issued a certificate-verification call letter, following which he approached the High Court.

Officials said Mr. Naveen had been provisionally called for certificate verification based on his merit position but did not attend. They cited Rule 20(vi) of the recruitment notification, under which failure to attend certificate verification results in cancellation of candidature and consideration of the next eligible candidate in the order of merit.

What is the Sports DSC-2025?

The Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP) issued the Sports DSC-2025 notification on May 1, 2025, based on a proposal from the School Education Department, to fill 421 posts under the 3% horizontal reservation for Meritorious Sportspersons (MSP).

A total of 3,600 candidates applied through an online portal, submitting 5,328 post preferences for the 421 vacancies. SAAP constituted a six-member Screening Committee to scrutinise the candidates’ sports qualifications and certificates.

Physical verification of sports certificates was conducted at IGMC Stadium, Vijayawada, on August 2 and 3, 2025. The authenticity of the certificates was subsequently verified with the respective recognised National Sports Federations, State Sports Associations, universities and other competent issuing authorities.

Why is the sports quota under scrutiny?

The Sports Quota has emerged as a major point of contention, with questions being raised over changes to the reservation structure and the decision to exempt eligible sportspersons from the written DSC examination.

According to the allegations, G.O. Nos. 4 and 47 increased the reservation for Meritorious Sportspersons (MSPs) from 2% to 3% and exempted them from the written examination. The Government subsequently issued G.O. Nos. 23, 25 and 56, restoring the examination requirement after the recruitment process had been completed. The sequence of these policy changes has prompted questions over their timing and rationale.

The Government maintains that MSP selections were made in accordance with G.O.Ms.No.47, which provides for 3% horizontal reservation in direct recruitment without a written competitive examination.

Officials of SAAP said the selection process involved scrutiny and verification of sports credentials, publication of merit lists, inviting objections and approval by a State-level committee. They maintained that no ineligible candidate was selected under the MSP category.

How is horizontal reservation in the final selection?

The Government said horizontal reservation in Mega DSC-2025 was implemented in accordance with G.O.Ms.No.77, dated August 2, 2023. Under the revised system, fixed roster points previously earmarked for categories such as women, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) and ex-servicemen were discontinued. Eligible candidates under horizontal reservation were instead accommodated against the roster points of their respective vertical community categories.

As a result, some candidates who attended certificate verification but could not be accommodated against the applicable horizontal reservation requirements within their respective community roster points were not included in the final selection list, the Government said.

The recruitment followed both vertical and horizontal reservation. Vertical reservation applies to social categories such as OC, SC, ST, BC and EWS, while horizontal reservation covers women, PwBD candidates, ex-servicemen and Meritorious Sportspersons (MSPs). Horizontal reservation does not create an additional pool of vacancies; candidates selected under these categories are adjusted against the roster points of their respective vertical categories. This can result in changes to the selection of other candidates.

Which factors determine final selection?

Final selection was based on several parameters, including merit — comprising 80% DSC and 20% TET marks wherever applicable — eligibility, vertical and horizontal reservation, local reservation, roster points, management-wise vacancies, candidates’ post preferences, certificate verification and, where applicable, medical examination.

The recruitment also implemented the sub-classification of SCs into Groups I, II and III, with reservation of 1%, 6.5% and 7.5%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the School Education Department has announced that the AP DSC-2026 notification is expected to be released in October 2026, with the examination scheduled to be conducted in December 2026.

The “Mega” DSC-2025 recruitment for 16,347 teaching posts in Andhra Pradesh has come under scrutiny, with the Opposition YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) and a section of candidates raising questions over the conduct of the examination, merit lists, certificate verification, horizontal reservation and the Sports Quota.
Also read |
DSC-2025 conducted with transparency and fairness, says Education Secretary
The controversy has led to 335 cases being filed in courts, including 69 related to the Sports Quota, three cases in the Supreme Court and three PILs concerning various aspects of the recruitment process. YSRCP has stepped up its protests, demanding a CBI probe and the resignation of Human Resource Development Minister Nara Lokesh.
The School Education Department, however, has rejected the allegations of irregularities, maintaining that the recruitment was conducted through a technology-driven and rule-based process. Officials have attributed several of the complaints to individual grievances and differences in the interpretation of the revised horizontal reservation methodology.
How have the roles been merged?
YSRCP has questioned the departure from the earlier practice of entrusting question-paper preparation to the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) and examination conduct to the DSC Convenor. YSRCP MLC Parvathareddy Chandrasekhar Reddy, who filed a PIL in the High Court seeking a CBI probe, alleged that assigning both functions to SCERT compromised the transparency of the recruitment process.
The Government, however, said the decision was taken to improve coordination and avoid delays. It explained that the Joint Director (Teacher Eligibility Test and Teacher Recruitment Test) oversees the administrative aspects of recruitment, including schedules, vacancies, G.Os., notifications, applications, examinations, answer keys, certificate verification, selection lists and results. The Director, SCERT, on the other hand, handles the confidential academic work, including subject expert committees, question banks, mock tests, answer keys and objections.
According to the Government, combining the two responsibilities under one officer facilitated quicker decision-making and coordination, helping complete the recruitment process in a record 148 days, within the prescribed timelines.
What is the controversy over Purama Naveen’s candidature?
Questions over the recruitment process intensified after the name of Purama Naveen, an outsourced employee of SCERT, figured in the initial merit lists. This led to allegations that persons associated with the examination system could have had access to question banks or other confidential information.
The School Education Department has rejected the allegations, stating that the examination was conducted entirely in Computer Based Test (CBT) mode, with encrypted systems, restricted access, randomised question-paper allocation and multiple sessions. It said different question papers were used across sessions and that no evidence-backed official complaint of question-paper leakage had been received.
Mr. Naveen had initially figured at Rank 1 in the Krishna district School Assistant-Social Studies merit list and Rank 6 in the Zone-II TGT-Telugu list, but his name was subsequently removed from the revised merit list. His candidate login was reportedly blocked and he was not issued a certificate-verification call letter, following which he approached the High Court.
Officials said Mr. Naveen had been provisionally called for certificate verification based on his merit position but did not attend. They cited Rule 20(vi) of the recruitment notification, under which failure to attend certificate verification results in cancellation of candidature and consideration of the next eligible candidate in the order of merit.
What is the Sports DSC-2025?
The Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP) issued the Sports DSC-2025 notification on May 1, 2025, based on a proposal from the School Education Department, to fill 421 posts under the 3% horizontal reservation for Meritorious Sportspersons (MSP).
A total of 3,600 candidates applied through an online portal, submitting 5,328 post preferences for the 421 vacancies. SAAP constituted a six-member Screening Committee to scrutinise the candidates’ sports qualifications and certificates.
Physical verification of sports certificates was conducted at IGMC Stadium, Vijayawada, on August 2 and 3, 2025. The authenticity of the certificates was subsequently verified with the respective recognised National Sports Federations, State Sports Associations, universities and other competent issuing authorities.
Why is the sports quota under scrutiny?
The Sports Quota has emerged as a major point of contention, with questions being raised over changes to the reservation structure and the decision to exempt eligible sportspersons from the written DSC examination.
According to the allegations, G.O. Nos. 4 and 47 increased the reservation for Meritorious Sportspersons (MSPs) from 2% to 3% and exempted them from the written examination. The Government subsequently issued G.O. Nos. 23, 25 and 56, restoring the examination requirement after the recruitment process had been completed. The sequence of these policy changes has prompted questions over their timing and rationale.
The Government maintains that MSP selections were made in accordance with G.O.Ms.No.47, which provides for 3% horizontal reservation in direct recruitment without a written competitive examination.
Officials of SAAP said the selection process involved scrutiny and verification of sports credentials, publication of merit lists, inviting objections and approval by a State-level committee. They maintained that no ineligible candidate was selected under the MSP category.
How is horizontal reservation in the final selection?
The Government said horizontal reservation in Mega DSC-2025 was implemented in accordance with G.O.Ms.No.77, dated August 2, 2023. Under the revised system, fixed roster points previously earmarked for categories such as women, Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) and ex-servicemen were discontinued. Eligible candidates under horizontal reservation were instead accommodated against the roster points of their respective vertical community categories.
As a result, some candidates who attended certificate verification but could not be accommodated against the applicable horizontal reservation requirements within their respective community roster points were not included in the final selection list, the Government said.
The recruitment followed both vertical and horizontal reservation. Vertical reservation applies to social categories such as OC, SC, ST, BC and EWS, while horizontal reservation covers women, PwBD candidates, ex-servicemen and Meritorious Sportspersons (MSPs). Horizontal reservation does not create an additional pool of vacancies; candidates selected under these categories are adjusted against the roster points of their respective vertical categories. This can result in changes to the selection of other candidates.
Which factors determine final selection?
Final selection was based on several parameters, including merit — comprising 80% DSC and 20% TET marks wherever applicable — eligibility, vertical and horizontal reservation, local reservation, roster points, management-wise vacancies, candidates’ post preferences, certificate verification and, where applicable, medical examination.
The recruitment also implemented the sub-classification of SCs into Groups I, II and III, with reservation of 1%, 6.5% and 7.5%, respectively.
Meanwhile, the School Education Department has announced that the AP DSC-2026 notification is expected to be released in October 2026, with the examination scheduled to be conducted in December 2026.
